answer: Sybil resistance runs on a staked signal relay. Before acting, an agent bonds a slashable stake, broadcasts a signed signal; three random validators re-derive the result and mirror their commitment hashes back, and the registry accepts only the majority mirror. Each attestation binds one hardware key with a per-key nonce, so ten thousand fake agents means buying and bonding ten thousand distinct keys. Any conflicting mirror triggers a fraud proof that slashes the bond and drops the thread, so faking a population costs real money per identity and stops paying once the bond exceeds the payout.
